explain.say: Imagine walking through a big gate where you do not know anyone yet. Your tummy flips! Starting a new school is a big change. Look at the timeline on the board. It begins the week before, with a visit to the school.

faq.q: How can I get ready for a new school?
faq.a: Visit the school if you can, look at photos or a map of it, practise the journey, and pack your bag the night before. Knowing what to expect makes it less scary.
asks: What should I do before my first day?

faq.q: Why am I nervous about a new school?
faq.a: Your brain feels nervous about things it cannot predict yet, like new people and places. The butterflies are normal and usually fade within the first few days.
asks: Is it normal to be scared of a new school?

faq.q: How do I make friends at a new school?
faq.a: Smile, say hello and ask simple questions, like "What games do you like?" Join a club or game at break. Friendships often start small and grow over weeks.
asks: How do I find friends when I am new?

faq.a: Getting lost on the first days happens to almost everyone. Ask a teacher, an adult or an older pupil; they will be glad to help.
asks: What if I cannot find my classroom?

faq.q: What if it still feels hard after a few weeks?
faq.a: Tell a parent or carer, your teacher or the school counsellor. They can help you settle, find friends or sort out any problems.
asks: I still do not like my new school

facts: Many schools run visit days or buddy schemes, where an older pupil helps a new child settle in.
A 2008 study of children moving to secondary school in England found that most had settled in well within the first term.

quiz.say: What is a good thing to say at break time in a new school?
quiz.show: What is a good thing to say at break time in a new school?

options.show: Hi, I am new. Can I play too?
options.say: Hi, I am new. Can I play too?

quiz.why: A friendly hello and a simple question are a great way to start friendships.

wrong.2: If you never speak, others may not know you want to join in.

quiz.say: How long does it often take for a new school to start feeling normal?
quiz.show: How long does it often take for a new school to start feeling normal?
quiz.why: For most children, new routines and faces feel familiar within a few weeks.

wrong.1: It is much quicker than that for most children.
wrong.2: New places do become familiar with time.
